input.quote: This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause triggers (material breach in 9.1, insolvency in 9.2, Vendor security/service/legal/IP failures in 9.3), and Sections 8.2 (180 days' non-renewal notice) and 27.3 (force-majeure exit) do not give a convenience right. No provision anywhere lets Customer terminate without cause during the three-year term, which is walk-away territory under the rule (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term). Vendor likewise has no convenience right, so only the Customer-side gap needs fixing; we propose the preferred position — 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2 — inserted as new Section 9.4 (the number is currently unused).

proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (new § 9.4)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs for three years but gives us no right to exit without cause, so we have added a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, consistent with Section 10.2. If Vendor needs more runway, we can discuss 60 days' notice, but we cannot accept a multi-year commitment with no convenience exit.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.
